subject.title: Follow-up: optimize fallback order + add model-input config guardrail

question: Should OpenClaw keep explicit operator-ordered fallback lists, add a benchmark-backed cost/latency/quality fallback policy, or split that policy into a narrower canonical issue while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/50287 owns the model-input guardrail?
rationale: Source inspection shows the current runtime treats fallback order as explicit operator intent, while tightening model-input validation can invalidate accepted custom provider metadata; automation cannot choose those product and compatibility tradeoffs.

options.title: Keep this as the broad tracker
options.body: Leave this issue open until maintainers publish or reject the benchmark-backed fallback policy, while using https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/50287 for the focused guardrail work.

options.title: Create a focused fallback-policy canonical
options.body: Open or restore a dedicated cost-first fallback-order issue and close this issue only after that item owns the remaining fallback-policy half.

options.title: Reject automatic ranking for now
options.body: Document that fallback order remains operator-controlled and continue only with explicit validation or diagnostics work in the narrower guardrail issues.

recommendation.title: Keep this as the broad tracker
recommendation.body: Leave this issue open until maintainers publish or reject the benchmark-backed fallback policy, while using https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/50287 for the focused guardrail work.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent is the strongest recent routing candidate across current fallback/config code and related validation work.
